title: Polynomial dependence of commuting scalar differential operators
notes: The theorem attributed to A. B. Shabat says \([L_n,L_m]=0\Rightarrow P(L_n,L_m)=0\). Its proof uses \(L_m\) on the solution space of \(L_ny=Ey\), but calls a polynomial of degree \(n+1\) the characteristic polynomial. Bernstein mentions an earlier polynomial-coefficient result without a title.
statement: For commuting scalar ordinary differential operators of positive orders \(n,m\), with complex analytic germs as coefficients and nonvanishing leading coefficients, there is a nonzero \(P(E,w)\in\mathbb C[E,w]\) such that \(P(L_n,L_m)=0\). The solution space of \(L_ny=Ey\) has dimension \(n\). In its initial-jet basis, the induced matrix \(M(E)\) of \(L_m\) has entries polynomial in \(E\), by repeated substitution of the differential equation. Thus \(P(E,w)=\det(wI-M(E))\) has degree \(n\) in \(w\), and Cayley--Hamilton gives the operator identity. Coprimality of \(n,m\) is unnecessary.
reconstruction: \ours\ The condensed initial-jet argument reconstructs the proof read in Krichever's Theorem~2.1; the notebook's exponential asymptotic sketch is not needed. The degree \(n+1\) is corrected to \(n\). The untitled 1967 reference mentioned by Bernstein was not independently identified.
fate: \citet[Theorem~1]{amitsur1958commutative} already yields algebraic dependence. The notebook proof is reproduced as \citet[Theorem~2.1]{krichever1977methods}; the Shabat attribution does not establish general priority.

title: The spectral curve and a normalized common eigenfunction
notes: The eigenvalues satisfy \(P(E,w)=0\), and a common eigenfunction normalized by \(\psi(x_0,P)=1\) is viewed as a function on the resulting algebraic curve.
statement: Take an irreducible component of the joint spectral curve and, when necessary, its normalization. If the generic simultaneous eigenspace is one-dimensional, the eigenline can locally be normalized by evaluation at \(x_0\), away from points where that evaluation vanishes. This gives a common eigenfunction meromorphic in the spectral point off the distinguished point at infinity, with a fixed divisor bounding its finite poles. A commuting pair of coprime positive orders is a sufficient rank-one situation. Higher generic rank requires vector-bundle data and does not yield one scalar normalized eigenfunction carrying the full information.
reconstruction: Generic rank, normalization of a possibly singular affine curve, and the excluded normalization zeros are supplied. The scalar construction is not asserted for every commuting pair merely because a polynomial relation exists.
fate: The rank-one and coprime-order argument is read in \citet[Section~2.2]{krichever1977methods}. It was developed in the speaker's 1976--1977 publications following these seminar reports.

title: Existence and uniqueness of the one-point Baker--Akhiezer function
notes: On a nonsingular algebraic curve \(X\) with marked \(P_0\), the notes prescribe an \(x\)-independent nonspecial divisor \(D\) of degree \(g\) and the expansion \(e^{k(x-x_0)}(1+\sum\xi_i(x)k^{-i})\). The local coordinate \(1/k\) is mistakenly said to be near \(x_0\).
statement:
Let \(X\) be a smooth compact complex curve of genus \(g\), \(P_\infty\in X\), \(z=k^{-1}\) a local coordinate there, and \(D\) a nonspecial effective divisor of degree \(g\), disjoint from \(P_\infty\). For \(x\) near \(x_0\), except possible exceptional parameter values, there is a unique function \(\psi(x,P)\), meromorphic on \(X\setminus\{P_\infty\}\) with poles bounded by \(D\), such that
     \[e^{-k(x-x_0)}\psi(x,P)=1+\sum_{j\geq1}\xi_j(x)k^{-j}\]
     is holomorphic at \(P_\infty\). At \(x=x_0\), nonspeciality and normalization give \(\psi=1\). For more general \(x\), the dependence may be meromorphic and the construction is used away from its parameter poles.
reconstruction: Compactness, disjointness and exceptional \(x\)-values are made explicit. The divisor bounds the poles: it cannot be the exact polar divisor for every \(x\), since \(\psi(x_0,\cdot)=1\).
fate: The lemma is read in \citet[pp.~291--292]{krichever1976zakharov}. Receipt on 8 October 1975 and presentation on 24 October do not independently prove public availability before the notebook's 20 October report.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established in the stated scope.

title: The function ring acts by commuting differential operators
notes: Every \(E\in\Lambda(X,P_0)\), meromorphic only at \(P_0\), is assigned a unique \(L_E\) with \(L_E\psi=E\psi\). Matching principal parts determines its coefficients, and \(E\mapsto L_E\) is a ring homomorphism.
statement:
For the smooth Baker--Akhiezer data of 1975-374.4, let \(A(X,P_\infty)\) be the ring of meromorphic functions with poles only at \(P_\infty\). For pole order \(n\geq2\), if
     \(E=c_nk^n+c_{n-1}k^{n-1}+c_{n-2}k^{n-2}+\cdots\), there is a unique scalar differential operator
     \(L_E=c_nD^n+c_{n-1}D^{n-1}+\sum_{j=0}^{n-2}u_j(x)D^j\)
     satisfying \(L_E\psi=E\psi\), with coefficients meromorphic in the allowed \(x\)-domain. For example,
     \(u_{n-2}=c_{n-2}-nc_n\xi'_1\).
     Constants act by \(L_E=c_0\); for pole order one the formula is \(L_E=c_1D+c_0\).
     The map is injective and obeys \(L_{E+F}=L_E+L_F\), \(L_{EF}=L_EL_F\); hence its image is commutative and order equals pole order for nonconstant \(E\).
reconstruction: After matching principal parts, the remainder has zero normalized leading term and the same allowed poles; Baker--Akhiezer uniqueness makes it vanish. The index bounds printed for \(u_i=Q(c_j,\xi_s^{(r)})\) cannot hold literally: already \(u_0\) for \(n=2\) depends on \(\xi'_1\).
fate: The construction is read in \citet[pp.~291--292]{krichever1976zakharov}; the coefficient example and ring statement are explicit in \citet[Sections~1--2]{krichever1977methods}.

title: Pole-order gaps and the genus sum
notes: Let \(n\) be the least positive pole order and \(s+\mu_sn\) an available order in residue class \(s\); then \(\sum_{s=1}^{n-1}\mu_s=g\).
statement: For a smooth genus-\(g\) curve and marked point, let \(H\subset\mathbb Z_{\geq0}\) be its Weierstrass semigroup of allowable pole orders. If \(n\) is its least positive element and \(w_s=s+\mu_sn\) is the \emph{least} element of \(H\) congruent to \(s\pmod n\), then the gaps in this residue class are \(s,s+n,\ldots,s+(\mu_s-1)n\). The gap theorem gives exactly \(g\) gaps, so \(\sum_s\mu_s=g\). Merely choosing an arbitrary available order in each residue class would not give this equality.
reconstruction: \ours\ The residue-class count is supplied explicitly. Minimality in each residue class is essential and is restored. The same semigroup records orders of the operators from 1975-374.5.
fate: This is the classical Riemann--Roch gap count applied to the function ring used in \citet[Section~2.2]{krichever1977methods}; the elementary residue-class count above explains the exact notebook formula.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established in the stated scope.

title: The claimed algebraic independence is impossible
notes: At a point in general position the notes assert \(g\) algebraically independent commuting operators.
statement: The function field of a curve has transcendence degree one. Therefore any two elements of the associated scalar differential-operator ring are algebraically dependent, and for \(g>1\) the asserted \(g\)-fold algebraic independence is impossible. At an ordinary point the gaps are \(1,\ldots,g\); one can instead choose algebra generators with pole orders \(g+1,\ldots,2g+1\), subject to algebraic relations. An alternative module description uses one pole-order-\(g+1\) function and a basis over its polynomial ring.
reconstruction: Algebra generators, module generators and algebraically independent elements are different notions. The notebook does not identify which of the first two was intended, so its numeral is not silently emended.
fate: The contradiction already follows from \citet[Theorem~1]{amitsur1958commutative} and the polynomial dependence of 1975-374.2. The curve-ring construction supplies the corrected interpretation.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established in the stated scope.

title: A genus criterion requires more than a list of operator orders
notes: An operator is called algebraic of genus \(g\) if it arises from the curve construction. An equivalence is then asserted with the existence of commuting operators of orders \(s+\mu_sn\), where \(\sum\mu_s=g\); the proof of sufficiency is only a short sketch.
statement: In the smooth rank-one construction, the least pole orders in each residue class provide the stated commuting partners and recover the genus by the gap count. In the reverse direction, a commutative ring of scalar operators gives a spectral curve and eigenfunction data. To identify it with the preceding smooth-curve construction one must control rank, the full ring rather than an arbitrary subalgebra, the compactification and possible singularities, and the divisor and normalization at infinity. A list of available orders is not itself this spectral data, and arbitrary nonminimal \(\mu_s\) do not determine genus.
reconstruction: This is a partial reconstruction of the claimed criterion. No exact if-and-only-if theorem with only the notebook's numerical hypotheses is asserted; in particular arithmetic and geometric genus cannot be silently interchanged in a singular case.
fate: The relevant classification appears in \citet[Section~2.2, Theorem~2.2]{krichever1977methods}. It verifies the spectral-data framework, not the exact abbreviated numerical criterion here.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The rank-one spectral classification is established; the notebook’s bare genus criterion remains only partially reconstructed.

title: Commutativity of the centralizer
notes: The report remarks that operators commuting with a pair commute with each other. A participant recorded as Limanov adds the polynomial-coefficient version: two operators commuting with a third commute mutually.
statement: For scalar ordinary differential operators over a characteristic-zero differential field with algebraically closed constant field, the centralizer of a positive-order operator is commutative. Thus two operators commuting with such an operator commute with one another; a pair is unnecessary. The qualifier matters: if the third operator is merely a scalar constant, every operator commutes with it, and the conclusion is false. For example \(D\) and multiplication by \(x\) both commute with \(I\), but \([D,x]=1\).
reconstruction: The hypothesis of a positive-order operator is supplied, covering the adjacent \(L_n\) setting. The tentatively read surname is retained without identifying a particular person or a new polynomial-coefficient paper.
fate: \citet[Theorem~1]{amitsur1958commutative} proves this stronger centralizer statement in 1958. The seminar intervention is expository in that setting.

title: The normalized theta formula and its missing factors
notes: The final formula has an exponential \(\exp\int_{P_0}^{P}\omega\) without \(x\), a theta quotient shifted by \(Ux\), and a theta series whose factors of \(2\pi i\) are inconsistent with the normalized periods.
statement:
Choose holomorphic differentials with \(a\)-periods \(\delta_{ij}\), period matrix \(B\), and Abel map \(\mathcal A(P_\infty)=0\). Set
     \[\theta(z\mid B)=\sum_{m\in\mathbb Z^g}\exp(\pi i\,m^TBm+2\pi i\,m^Tz),\qquad \operatorname{Im}B>0.\]
     Let \(d\Omega\) have zero \(a\)-periods, only a double pole at \(P_\infty\), and principal part \(dk=-dz/z^2\); normalize its regularized integral by \(\Omega(P)=k+O(k^{-1})\). Put \(U_j=(2\pi i)^{-1}\int_{b_j}d\Omega\), and choose \(Z\) so that \(\theta(\mathcal A(P)+Z)\) has zero divisor \(D\). With \(t=x-x_0\), on the set where the denominator is nonzero,
     \[\psi(x,P)=e^{t\Omega(P)}
       \frac{\theta(\mathcal A(P)+tU+Z)\,\theta(Z)}
       {\theta(\mathcal A(P)+Z)\,\theta(tU+Z)}.\]
     This has the required normalized exponential expansion and \(\psi(x_0,P)=1\).
reconstruction: The parameter factor in the exponential, the normalization factor depending only on \(x\), the regularization at the pole, the sign of the second-kind principal part, and the consistent theta convention are all supplied explicitly. They cannot be recovered by treating an integral starting at its double pole as an ordinary convergent integral.
fate: The theta construction and normalization at the marked point are read in \citet[Section~1, pp.~189--190]{krichever1977methods}; the notebook has omitted essential factors.
